documents.title: Project Helios — public-records digitisation
sections: Helios digitises the paper public-records register held across four regional offices. The programme scans, OCRs and indexes roughly 1.2 million pages so that the register can be searched instead of retrieved by hand.

The largest risk is legacy data corruption on ingest: pages captured out of order lose their file context permanently. Every record is checksummed against the source register before the paper copy is released for storage.
Discovery completed on 2026-02-15 and pilot ingest is in progress. Go-live is planned for 2026-09-30, with a four-week contingency held against vendor scanning delays.
Budget is $225,000 across scanning and OCR, platform engineering, and assurance. Assurance is deliberately funded as a separate line so it cannot be traded away against schedule pressure.

documents.title: Project Borealis — grants payment reconciliation
sections: Borealis reconciles grant payments against acquittal reports for eleven programmes that currently reconcile by spreadsheet. The goal is one reconciliation ledger with a per-payment audit trail.
Duplicate acquittals are the dominant risk. Two programmes accept acquittals through both a portal and email, so the same claim can enter twice under different reference formats and clear twice.
The pilot covers three programmes only. Extending to the remaining eight is a separate decision that depends on whether the pilot's exception rate falls below two percent.

documents.title: Project Meridian — service-request triage
sections: Meridian classifies inbound service requests so they reach the right team without a manual triage queue. Requests arrive by web form, phone transcript and email in roughly equal volumes.
Phone transcripts are the weakest input: they carry no structured subject line, so classification depends entirely on the transcript body, and short calls are frequently unclassifiable.
Misrouted requests are worse than unrouted ones, because a misroute restarts the response clock silently. Anything the classifier is not confident about is held for human triage rather than guessed.
The measure of success is the share of requests that reach the correct team on the first attempt, sampled weekly against a human-labelled set.
A quarterly review checks the labelled sample for drift: if the request mix shifts, the classifier is re-evaluated before the next quarter's targets are set.
